IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT  NAINITAL  Leave to Appeal No. 285 of 2024  With  Government Appeal No. 179 of 2024 State of Uttarakhand ... Applicant  Versus Gaurav & Another ... Respondents  Mr. K.S. Bora, Deputy Advocate General, with  Mr. R.K. Joshi, Brief Holder for the  State/appellant.

sentences.text:
12.7.2024 Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
(Per: Hon'ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) IA/1/2024 (Delay Condonation Application)
Present appeal has been preferred with the delay of 220 days.
We have perused the application seeking condonation of delay in filing the present appeal.
We are satisfied that the delay has properly been explained.
Therefore, application, seeking condonation of delay, is allowed.
Delay is condoned.

SPLA/285/2024 (Application Seeking Leave to Appeal) By this petition under Section 378(3) of CrPC, State/petitioner is seeking leave to appeal against the judgment/order dated 14.8.2023,
passed by Additional Sessions Judge/FTC, Rudrapur, District Udham Singh Nagar, thereby acquitting the respondent no. 1 from the charges framed against him under Sections 363, 366, 323,
376(2), 120B read with 34 IPC and Section 4 of the POCSO Act and respondent no. 2 from the charges framed against him under Sections 363, 366, 120B read with 34 IPC and Section 17 of the POCSO Act.
2. It is the case of the prosecution that age of victim at the time of alleged incident was 14 years.

It has come in the evidence of Principal (PW2) of the school concerned, as noticed by the Trial Court while dealing first with the issue of victim's age, that birth certificate of the prosecutrix was not produced and her date of birth was recorded in the school, where she took admission directly in Class V, on the basis of affidavit of her father (who was not examined); PW2 deposed that father of prosecutrix had stated in the affidavit that earlier the prosecutrix was being homeschooled; victim's mother PW4 deposed in her testimony that it was she who had gone to admit the victim in the State Of Uttarakhand vs Gaurav & Another on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199559982/
1 school in Class V and her admission was accepted on the basis of transfer certificate, issued by the school she was earlier attending to; and neither the victim PW3 nor her mother PW4 stated in their testimony as to on what basis they are stating that the age of prosecutrix on the date of incident was 14 years.

Trial Court relied upon a judgment of this Court, rendered in the case of Suraj Pal v. State of Uttarakhand, to say that age determination has to be on the basis of settled statutory criteria.

sentences.text:
3. While appreciating the evidence, the Trial Court also noticed that the case of the prosecution was that it was the first accused (Gaurav), who telephoned the victim and invited her to see the fair,
however, the victim, in her cross-examination, has admitted that she had gone to see the fair on her own wishes; that, as per the case of prosecution, the victim remained with the accused right from 13.9.2019 to 15.9.2019 and travelled with them from Kashipur to Moradabad and from Moradabad to Dehradun and the first accused (Gaurav) committed rape on her in his house at Moradabad and his family members were present in the house and thereafter raped her in Dehradun and then dropped her at Moradabad railway station, from where she returned in a train to her house in Kashipur on 15.9.2019 and narrated the entire story to her mother, however, the victim did not raise any alarm anywhere; even the FIR could be lodged on 19.9.2019; and that she could have easily raised the alarm had she been abducted/kidnapped or subjected to rape.
4. It is also to be noticed that prosecutrix and accused knew each other since before the alleged incident.

It is also to be noticed that the victim was missing since 13.9.2019, but no missing report was lodged and even the FIR could be lodged on 19.9.2019, though the victim returned back on 15.9.2019 and narrated the story to her mother and there is absolutely no explanation for such delay.
It is also to be noticed that earlier also, prosecutrix had made similar allegations against one Mr. Kaka @ Jaspal and, during trial, she and her mother turned hostile.

5. Since prosecutrix was major and she remained with the accused for more than two days and travelled to different places, where she could have easily raised the alarm, but she did not do so, and even the FIR was lodged after six days, therefore, reasonable doubt has occurred about the genuineness of the prosecution story.
Thus, we are of the view that the Trial Court has rightly returned the finding of acquittal.
It is settled law that the Appellate Court may overrule or otherwise disturb the finding of acquittal only if it has very substantial and compelling reasons to do so.

6. Since no arguable points have been raised nor any material has been brought to our notice, which may require deeper consideration and re-appreciation or reconsideration of evidence, we refuse to grant leave to appeal.
Leave petition is dismissed.
Government appeal also stands dismissed accordingly.
(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
